steps.text: Electricity does many jobs in our homes. Let's sort appliances by what electricity does in each.
Look at each appliance and decide what electricity gives it — heat, light, sound, or movement.
A heater and iron make heat; a bulb makes light; a fan and mixer make movement; a radio makes sound.
Electricity is useful because it easily turns into heat, light, sound, and motion — that's why it powers almost everything.

coach.mission: Sort appliances by what electricity does in each.
whenStuck: Ask: does this appliance make heat, light, sound, or movement?
A fan moves; a bulb lights; a heater warms.
whenWrong: Match the appliance to its effect — a heater makes heat, a fan makes movement.
Electricity can become heat, light, sound, or motion.
whenCorrect: Right — that's what electricity does in that appliance.
Good — electricity changes into many useful forms.
coach.done: You've sorted the uses of electricity. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
